blocks.text: A briefing for the client sponsor on the opening phase of the review. The engagement began on {{fact:f:E-2010-001.start}} and is scoped to run about four months; this deck covers where the work stands in its early weeks.
What we set out to answer

items: Where the supply chain of {{fact:f:E-2010-001.client}} earns its keep today, and where it costs more than it returns.
How cost, service levels, and inventory compare with a well-run operation of similar size.
Which improvements are worth pursuing, and what each would ask of the organization.
We are in the opening phase: building a faithful picture of the supply chain as it runs today.
The flow from supplier to point of use is being traced end to end.
First data requests are out to the client team, and the cost and inventory picture is being assembled behind them.

blocks.text: What the baseline is beginning to show

items: The documented process and the process as actually run differ in a few predictable places.
Inventory is carried unevenly across the network, and some of it buys less protection than its cost suggests.
A few figures still rest on data we are verifying; we mark those plainly rather than lean on them.
Michael Walker, Engagement Manager, runs the work day to day and holds the relationship.
Deborah Gordon, Associate, leads the benchmarking and the cost and inventory analysis.
Daniel Leach, Research Associate, assembles and verifies the underlying data.
Sandra Flores, Chief Operating Officer, is our sponsor on the client side.
Close out the baseline and the benchmark over the coming weeks.
Frame the handful of improvements the analysis supports, each with its cost and its likely return.
Return to you with those options before any direction is fixed.
